claim: § What It Is: quadratic "has changing slope but continuous first derivative" and is "much smoother for audio"; § 3 Pitch Detection gives a parabolic-peak formula. A piece checks both: the three-point parabola as written is not slope-continuous from one segment to the next, and the peak formula's sign points the wrong way against the standard (a - c)/(a - 2b + c) form.

pieces.what: Drag three points, see the parabola through them; then chain segments along a waveform and plot the slope at each joint, testing the 'no sharp corner' claim
Read a single-cycle table at a gliding pitch with none / linear / quadratic / cubic interpolation, hear each and see its alias spectrum, testing 'quadratic is the sweet spot'
pieces.walks_up_from: one sine table read at one fixed ratio

pieces.section: 3. Pitch Detection via Parabolic Interpolation on FFT Peaks
pieces.what: A sine between two bins, the three magnitudes, and the refined estimate from the page's formula and from the standard one, showing which lands on the true frequency
pieces.walks_up_from: one sine exactly on a bin

pieces.what: A glide to a target by quadratic ramp and by a PID or second-order spring, heard back to back, testing whether overshoot sounds 'alive'
